messages:
Maria R.: Quick sync — for service->service auth are we converging on narrow capability tokens (short‑lived JWTs) or keeping project-scoped API keys with RBAC? Need tradeoffs + a migration sketch.
Hao L.: Capability tokens give true least-priv and easy revocation, but add complexity (token service, refresh flows). Project keys are simpler for customers but hard to revoke per-action.
Devon K.: Agreed. Project keys map nicely to existing proxy routing and billing, fewer moving pieces. Main risk = key sprawl and difficulty limiting scope to a single endpoint/action.
Anuj P.: From product POV some customers (CI, infra) expect long-lived keys. We should support both patterns but prefer a default that reduces blast radius. Hybrid sounds reasonable.
Hao L.: Proposed pattern: long-lived "anchor" API key that can mint short-lived capability tokens via token-exchange. Capability tokens carry precise claims: {
  "iss": "redwood-token",
  "sub": "svc-A",
  "aud": "svc-B",
  "scope": ["write:model:123", "invoke:inference"],
  "exp": 168
}
Devon K.: +1 on exchange. Also require token binding: either mTLS peer cert or include a KMS-signed key id (kid) so tokens can't be replayed from a different host.
Maria R.: How do we handle delegation (A calls B on behalf of user U)? Does capability token carry "act_as"? How to prevent transitive delegation?
Hao L.: Keep delegation explicit and single-hop: token can include an "act_as" claim with limited TTL and audience check. Reject tokens that were themselves minted from another delegated token (no transitive delegation). Simplified rule: allow delegation depth = 1.
Devon K.: Also enforce server-side checks: B must validate audience, scope intersection, and that "act_as" identity exists in our identity service. Log an audit event for every delegated call.
Anuj P.: Migration plan idea:
1) Build token service (mint, exchange, revoke, introspect) behind feature flag.
2) Proxy support: accept both API keys and capability tokens; prefer tokens when present.
3) SDKs: add token-exchange helper with retries + caching.
4) Opt-in customers get tokens first; enable org-wide after opt-in telemetry looks good.
Maria R.: Can you share a minimal token-exchange curl example for SDK teams?
Hao L.: Sure:

```
POST /v1/token/exchange
Authorization: Bearer <anchor_api_key>
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "audience": "svc-B",
  "scope": ["invoke:inference"],
  "ttl": 60
}

Response: 200 { "access_token": "ey...", "expires_in": 60 }
```

Devon K.: Ops notes: we need revocation lists for long-lived anchors and an introspect endpoint for proxies that can't validate JWTs locally. Also rate-limit mint endpoints to avoid abuse.
Anuj P.: Metrics to track: token_mint_rate, token_exchange_errors, revocations, failed_audience_checks, delegated_call_count. Also rollout health dashboards.
Maria R.: I'll capture this as a follow-up to the RFC. Small ask: eng-platform & SDK teams, please add a small helper to the JS/Go SDKs to do exchange+cache.
auth-bot: RFC issue created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/issues/842 — added label: authn-authz/token-exchange
Maria R.: Thanks — scheduling a 30min follow-up tomorrow to finalize constraints and canary plan.
